The Fear of Hadhrat Abu Haashim bin Utba bin Rabee'Ah Qurashi (RA)
The Incident with Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) at the time of death

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) came to visit Hadhrat Abu Haashim bin Utba (RA) when he fell ill. Finding him in tears, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) asked, "What makes you weep dear uncle? Are you suffering with pain or are you grieving over leaving this world?" "Not at all," he replied, "I am crying because Rasulullaah ﷺ had given us explicit advice that we failed to adhere to." "What was that advice?" enquired Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). Hadhrat Abu Haashim (RA) replied, "I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'It is sufficient only to possess a servant and a conveyance to use in the path of Allaah.' Today I find that I have accumulated plenty of wealth." A narration of Razeen states that after the demise of Hadhrat Abu Haashim bin Utba (RA), all his assets were evaluated thirty Dirhams. This even included a dish that he used for kneading dough and for eating.[^1]
Fear of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jaraah (RA) and his Weeping Over Worldly Prosperity

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Hasanah Muslim bin Akyas
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Hasanah Muslim bin Akyas the freed slave of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir reports that when someone once went to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jaraah (RA), he found him weeping. "What makes you weep, O Abu Ubaydah?" he asked. Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) replied, "I am weeping because Rasulullaah ﷺ once made mention of the conquests and spoils of war that Allaah would grant the Muslims. He also made mention of (conquering) Shaam and then said, 'O Abu Ubaydah! If your life is prolonged (to see the times of these conquests), three servants will be enough for you; one servant to serve you, one to travel with you and another for your family to serve them. At that time, three animals will be enough for you; one to ride, one to transport your goods and another for your servant.' Now I see that my house is full of servants and that my stables are full of animals and horses. How will I meet Rasulullaah ﷺ after this? Rasulullaah ﷺ also said to us, 'The most beloved and closest of you to me is the one who meets me in the condition that he left me.'"[^2]

Tirmidhi, Nasa'ee, Ibn Maajah and Ibn Hibbaan, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.184). Baghawi and Ibnus Sakan have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.4 Pg.201). Haakim has also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.149).
Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.253) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.73).
